title: chat.post_system_message
description: Write ONE system line into a conversation, from another service. {"conversation_id", "body", "client_msg_id"?} -> {"message_id", "seq", "conversation_id"}. Deliberately narrow: it can only post with sender=null and kind=system, so it cannot be used to say something as a person. A general chat.post_message would be exactly that — a bus-reachable way to put words in a user's mouth, in a product where the thread is the record of a deal. The body is a marker key the reader renders (the convention chat's own lines already use: chat.support.assigned, video.call.ended:188), never a rendered sentence: a rendered string freezes one language and one number format into a row that outlives both, and the reader's locale is not the writer's. client_msg_id is the existing per-conversation idempotency key — pass a deterministic one derived from the fact being recorded and an at-least-once caller writes one line, not a line per redelivery. An unknown conversation_id raises rather than answering silently: a caller that could not record what happened must find out.

body.description: The system line. A dot-namespaced marker key, with its one argument after a colon where it has one (video.call.ended:188).

client_msg_id.description: Idempotency key, unique per conversation. Omit and a redelivery writes a second line.
